about: The golden set of the letter checks (#78): invented people, postings and letter sentences, each labelled with what the checks must say. Run before a change to a prompt or to a claim rule ships: tests/test_letter_evals.py. Add a case for every false alarm or missed claim found; never change a label to make a run pass. The inv-* cases were written before the #109 rules, but many of their sentences are also development rows in tests/test_claims.py, so their recall is a development number, not a held-out one; a fresh held-out batch should come from another writer. A case with "gap" is a known miss: it keeps its true label and runs as a strict expected failure, so a fix shows at once. The h113-* cases (#113) are held-out: another writer wrote them before the #113 code, and they must never be copied into tests/test_claims.py. The wording of some h113-* cases was seen during development, so their recall counts as development, not held-out: exact copies h113-1n-dev-course, h113-4-dev-present-labs, h113-6-acc-fluent; near copies h113-1n-dev-reviewed-posting, h113-1n-care-course, h113-2n-dev-new-subject, h113-4n-dev-tool-for-slack, h113-4n-acc-macro-for-excel, h113-5n-dev-python-version, h113-6-dev-native-speaker, h113-6n-dev-company, h113-6n-acc-fluent-excel. The h113r-* cases (#113, fix round) are hard negatives and true positives written after the first #113 code, for past-participle openings, requirement wording and the English exemption. The h131-* cases (#131) are held-out: written before the #131 code, for fresh participle frames about the employer, true positives in new frames, misplaced, figures and borrowed, and the known misses of #113 in new wording; the ones the code got wrong then are gaps. The guard in tests/test_letter_evals.py compares every h113 and h131 sentence with each string in tests/test_claims.py by its words (lower case, no punctuation, difflib ratio of 0.8 or more), so a near copy is caught, not only an exact one. The fuzzy guard found two near copies of development rows, h113-4n-acc-employed-known and h113-7n-dev-cv; both were rewritten in #131 as fresh held-out sentences. The guard now exempts nothing (no length pre-filter, and a held-out sentence that is most of a longer string counts as a copy): the cases listed above as seen during development stay as history, and the six that the stricter guard flagged were rewritten in #131 as fresh sentences with the same label (h113-1n-dev-course, h113-1n-dev-trained-in, h113-4-dev-present-labs, h113-4n-acc-macro-for-excel, h113-6-acc-fluent, h131-d8-acc-german-c1). The h131-e* cases measure the cost of the term-based exception: an employer description that opens with a participle phrase holding a year and a tool the CV lacks still reads as a claim; they are accepted false alarms. The h142-* cases (#142) are held-out: another writer wrote them before the fix for first-person and CV-style claims and for wishes that end at a comma before done work, and they must never be copied into tests/test_claims.py; the guard in tests/test_letter_evals.py covers them. The h142 cases the code missed then are gaps. The h143-* cases (#143) are held-out: another writer wrote them blind after the #142 code, for first-person claims of knowing, being and doing, duties, CV-style openers and claims after a wish, with hard negatives in the same shapes, and they must never be copied into tests/test_claims.py; the guard in tests/test_letter_evals.py covers them. The h143 cases the code got wrong are gaps. The cases h143-17 and h143-28 were shown to the fixer in the #143 fix round, so they count as development; the blind held-out numbers are the other 28 cases: claimed false alarms 0/11, claimed recall 14/17 (the three misses are known gaps). The h149-* cases (#149) are held-out: another writer wrote them before the #149 code, and they must never be copied into tests/test_claims.py; the guard in tests/test_letter_evals.py covers them. They cover the impact kind (a first-person sentence with a vague result the CV does not back; a wish, the company's own product and plain CV work are clean) and the misplaced kind for a term the CV names only under SKILLS. Learning ("I learned about Docker", "picked up") counts as no misplaced work. The case h149-12 ("picked up ... basics") was seen during the #149 fix and its words were added to the learning list, so its recall counts as development, not held-out; the cases h149-01 to h149-28 are spent after this round. The h149-29 to h149-52 cases are a second held-out batch for #149, written by another writer before the next code fix, for the person office (a non-developer CV with tools, soft skills and languages under SKILLS): misplaced tools at a former employer against soft skills and languages at an employer, impact across two sentences, intensifiers outside the usual ones, feelings and self-improvement, and results the CV itself backs.
